snapshot.title: TNPSC Unit 8: Later Pandyas & Nayaks
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC Unit 8 Hook: Sundara Pandyan: Greatest. Marco Polo: Kayal. Nayak: Palayam (72). Ariyanatha: Minister. Madurai: Nayak capital.

quick_notes.title: Later Pandyas (13th Century)
quick_notes.detail: Greatest: Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan. Second Pandyan Empire. Control over Pearl fishery.
quick_notes.explanation: The Later Pandyas refer to the Pandya dynasty that ruled in South India during the 13th century. The greatest king of this period was Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan. His reign is known as the Second Pandyan Empire, which means it was the second major period of power for the Pandya kingdom. Under him, the Pandya kingdom gained control over the pearl fishery, which was the industry of collecting pearls from oysters in the sea along the coasts of present-day Tamil Nadu and northern Sri Lanka.

quick_notes.title: Foreign Accounts
quick_notes.detail: Marco Polo (Venetian) and Wassaf (Persian) visited Kayal (Thoothukudi) and praised the wealth and horse trade.
quick_notes.explanation: Marco Polo was a Venetian traveler from Venice in Italy, and Wassaf was a Persian historian from Persia, which is modern-day Iran. Both of these foreign visitors came to the port town of Kayal, a place that is now called Thoothukudi in the state of Tamil Nadu. While there, they wrote in their accounts that Kayal was very wealthy and that it was a major center for trading horses. These descriptions

quick_notes.title: Madurai Nayaks
quick_notes.detail: Established by Viswanatha Nayak (under Vijayanagar). Introduced the "Palayakarar System" (72 Palayams).
quick_notes.explanation: The Madurai Nayaks were a dynasty that ruled the Madurai region in southern India. They were established by a ruler named Viswanatha Nayak, who was appointed by the larger Vijayanagar Empire. The Vijayanagar Empire was a powerful kingdom that controlled much of South India during that time. Viswanatha Nayak introduced the Palayakarar

quick_notes.title: Thirumalai Nayak
quick_notes.detail: Greatest Nayak ruler. Built the Thirumalai Nayak Mahal at Madurai. Renovated Meenakshi Temple.
quick_notes.explanation: Thirumalai Nayak was the most powerful ruler of the Nayak dynasty, which was a line of kings who ruled parts of southern India after the Vijayanagara Empire declined. He is famous for building the Thirumalai Nayak Mahal, which is a large palace in the city of Madurai, in the state of Tamil Nadu. He also renovated the Meenakshi Temple, which is a famous Hindu temple in Madurai dedicated to the goddess Meenakshi and her husband, Lord Sundareswarar. The word "renovated" means he repaired and improved the temple, adding new parts to make it more beautiful. His rule is remembered for these grand building projects that still stand today.

quick_notes.title: Social Structure
quick_notes.detail: Rise of temple-centric society. Development of Tamil literature under Saiva Siddhanta.
quick_notes.explanation: During the early medieval period in South India, society became centered around temples, which were not just places of worship but also the main hubs for economic, cultural, and political activities. This means that the temple controlled land, collected taxes, organized festivals, and provided jobs, making it the most important institution in a village or town. At the same time, Tamil literature grew and flourished under the influence of Saiva Siddhanta, which is a major school of Hindu philosophy that focuses on the worship of the god Shiva and explains the nature of the soul, God, and the world. The Saiva Siddhanta philosophy provided the themes and ideas for many religious poems and devotional works written during this period. As a result, the society was deeply religious, with the temple acting as the center of daily life and literature serving to spread and explain these religious beliefs.
